recipes.name: Pork Tenderloin Diablo
ingredients_raw: salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Season pork with salt and black pepper.

Heat oil in an ovenproof skillet over high heat. Add pork; cook until browned on one side, 3 to 4 minutes. Flip pork; transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Cook until pork browned and still slightly pink in center, 20 to 25 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C). Transfer pork to a plate.

Discard any excess oil from skillet. Place skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken broth; bring to a boil, scraping any browned bits off bottom of skillet. Whisk in cream, horseradish, Dijon mustard, and cayenne pepper; continue cooking until reduced to a thick sauce, 3 to 4 minutes. Off heat, whisk in cold butter, then stir in chives.
Slice pork into 1/2-inch slices; top with sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Tenderloin Diablo
raw_recipe.description: This is a great pork recipe. Mustard is a classic with pork, but when you add the extra zing of horseradish and cayenne, and then smooth it out with a little cream and butter, well, it’s devilishly delicious.

review.reviewBody: I love this method for cooking the pork. Be careful with the salt on the meat though - between the salt on the meat and the salt in the broth & mustard it left the sauce too salty.

This is a weekly meal in our house. My only change is that I adapted it for an instant pot. 6 minutes on high with 15 minute release. It takes a little longer to cook down the sauce on saute mode, and I'm impatient, so I usually add some xanthan gum to thicken it. I'm sure you could do the same with corn starch or flour.

This is a fantastic recipe. I make this verbatim aside from the fact that I brown all sides of the tenderloin in my cast iron skillet. I put my accurate meat thermometer in and pop it in the oven. I remove at @ 137 degrees and wrap in foil while I finish up the sauce. I always make this with mashed potatoes and learned the first time to start the potatoes before browning the pork! The last thing I do is slice the juicy pork. This is excellent with asparagus or broccoli!

OMG, the sauce is divine! I'll admit I used a rub that I use on many of my beef and pork roasts that always lends an outstanding base flavor (it is from Joel Manthel's "Herb Rubbed Sirloin Tip Roast". I always slather the meat with some olive oil, work the rub into the meat, and let it sit on the counter for about an hour before cooking. Chef's John's cooking time and treatment are spot on though. I used a cast iron for the process, and highly recommend it. Because I had two tenderloins that were heavy in the middle, I did take the temp up to 153 before plating and tenting while I made the sauce. I tripled the sauce, and boy I'm glad I did. The sauce is a superstar! Thanks Chef John for being my superstar for so many great recipes!

Excellent method to cook tenderloins and the sauce was lovely. Had 2 large tenderloins so tripled the sauce. Could not really taste the horseradish, and I had a new jar, although it wasn't "extra-hot". Added some more at the end. Next time don't add the horseradish until after simmering since boiling it mellows it's flavor. Didn't have chives. I don't think I let the sauce the reduce enough but it was still very tasty. Reheating worked well by using a small saucepan, adding a splash of cream and reheating sauce with the pork gently just until it came up to temp.

Marinated the meat with equal parts soy sauce, dijon, and EVOO (with garlic) for about 24 hours. The meat cooked this way was super tender and flavorful! Used regular horseradish because that's what I had and didn't include the cayenne. It was delicious! The sauce was amazing over Perfect Polenta. Served with green beans. Easy enough for a week day but impressive enough for guests.

Yum! Can honestly give 5 stars as prepared as directed. My husband doesn’t tolerate heat / so didn’t use horseradish and decreased cayenne by half. I didn’t have chives so added a little chopped red onion with the cream ( used 3tbsp 2% milk with 1tbsp as i didn’t have cream and sliced mushrooms as one reviewer suggested). It was delicious! Update 6/5/24: Made just as before but I hadn’t made in a while. My husband said “Why make this any other way-It’s cooke perfectly!” I roasted along with Simple Roasted Butternut Squash also on this site. Thank you!

So glad I doubled the sauce recipe! Sauce if phenomenal. I cooked the pork in my new Gourmia air fryer. Juiciest pork tenderloin EVER. I had to get some bread just to soak up the leftover sauce on my plate.

OMG! I've made this twice now and all I can say is this has got to be one of the best sauces you'll find anywhere! Put this on shoe leather and you'll gladly tear into it. 
My advice. Follow the directions as written and double or triple the volume. We put this on a bed of noodles (egg) and we did rice. Both times we wanted more but it's just enough to bang the tenderloin and not enough for the bedding. 
Another note we noticed was it goes exceedingly well over or with fresh asparagus. The two just get together so well that I'm looking to modify this so I can make a whole new dish out of it.
Don't hesitate on this one. It is wonderful.

I will definitely will make this again. The pork was so tender and the sauce very good. My husband thought it was great and said I can make this anytime for him. I did make a couple of changes. I am on a low saturated fat diet so I eliminated the cream. As a result, I used vegetable broth instead of chicken broth to give it a creamier texture. Also, because of the need for lower saturated fat, I used Blue Bonnet. I am sure that using the cream and butter would make a richer sauce, but this one was very good.

This was superb! I took others' advice and did not use salt on the pork as the Dijon provides a LOT of salt in the sauce. And I definitely doubled the sauce recipe. It had a wonderful, mellow heat that beautifully complemented the pork. And the mashed potatoes. And the roasted carrots. It was so good, I decided to lick my plate clean.
This was delicious! Followed the directions and made no changes.
Whenever I have a small dinner party I make this as “my specialty”. Only change I suggest is double/triple the sauce and cook it separately as it takes forever to reduce to a thick “gravy”.

One of tho rare recipes that’s great right out of the gate! The only change I made was increasing the cayenne from 1/4tsp to 1/2 tsp, as I thought the cayenne flavor might get lost between the hot horseradish and Dijon mustard. I recommend this minor tweak, but other than that, I wouldn’t change a thing!

Chef's Kiss This was amazing and my picky teenager ate it. I was worried she wouldn't like the pan sauce- I also have a picky SO and he ate two helpings. I would def use low sodium chicken broth next time but that was my ONLY complaint. I roasted off some sweet potatoes and sauteed up some green beans with it HOMERUN PS- Super easy and quick, I could do this on a weeknight
I made it according to the recipe and my family loved it. I will certainly be trying it again soon.
So easy, fast and delicious! Great for company. I don’t do any modifications good as is.
Delicious! Used regular horseradish but other than that, follow to the letter. Such an easy dinner but fit for company.

The whole family loved it! Thickening definitely took longer than suggested. I can't figure out why mine came out so salty-tasting, but it can't be the recipe's fault; I'll either omit salting the tenderloin, salt by hand and not by grinder, or only salt one side.
I make this often and love it. I love salt, so I use salted butter and salt the meat and everything.
